claim: A pre-release version has lower precedence than the associated normal (release) version with the same major.minor.patch.
sub_question: What is precedence of pre-release vs same version with build metadata only?
evidence: SemVer clause 9 states pre-release versions rank below their associated normal version; clause 11.3 restates this for equal major.minor.patch.
quote_or_anchor: Pre-release versions have a lower precedence than the associated normal version. ... When major, minor, and patch are equal, a pre-release version has lower precedence than a normal version: Example: 1.0.0-alpha < 1.0.0.

claim: Build metadata is ignored for precedence; a version with build metadata only has the same precedence as the plain normal version.
sub_question: What is precedence of pre-release vs same version with build metadata only?
evidence: SemVer clause 10 requires build metadata to be ignored when determining precedence; versions differing only in build metadata share precedence.
quote_or_anchor: Build metadata MUST be ignored when determining version precedence. Thus two versions that differ only in the build metadata, have the same precedence.
notes: Therefore X.Y.Z+build has the same precedence as X.Y.Z.

claim: Build metadata does not figure into precedence calculation; only major minor patch and pre-release identifiers do.
sub_question: What is precedence of pre-release vs same version with build metadata only?
evidence: SemVer clause 11.1 excludes build metadata from the ordered identifiers used for precedence.
quote_or_anchor: Precedence MUST be calculated by separating the version into major, minor, patch and pre-release identifiers in that order (Build metadata does not figure into precedence).
notes: Combined with C001 and C002: pre-release < same core with build-only.

claim: Therefore a version with a pre-release identifier has lower precedence than the same major.minor.patch with build metadata only.
sub_question: What is precedence of pre-release vs same version with build metadata only?
evidence: Synthesis of clauses 9 10 and 11: e.g. 1.0.0-alpha is below 1.0.0 and build is ignored so 1.0.0+meta equals 1.0.0; hence 1.0.0-alpha < 1.0.0+meta.
quote_or_anchor: Pre-release versions have a lower precedence than the associated normal version. Build metadata MUST be ignored when determining version precedence. ... (Build metadata does not figure into precedence).
notes: Order: pre-release version < same version with build metadata only (equal to normal).
